subject: Mutual plan: reserve runway & GPU tranche schedule for Acme Health
messages:
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@acmehealth.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial ask — capacity runway and procurement lead times

Hi Vivek / Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're starting to map out procurement windows for 2027 and want to capture a mutual plan that ties evaluation milestones to GPU reservation tranches. High level:

- We need predictable lead times for Dedicated / Private deployments (on-prem gateway + VPC).
- Procurement needs an earliest ship-by date to include in the capital request.
- Engineering wants guidance on pool sizing by phase so we can plan integration tests.

Attached is a short list of our evaluation requirements and compliance constraints (acme-eval-reqs.pdf). Can you propose a MAP skeleton with milestone dates, minimum tranche sizes, and slip/accelerate points?

Thanks,
Maria
Maria Gomez
Head of Platform Strategy
Acme Health

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Cc: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask — capacity runway and procurement lead times

Hi Maria — thanks for the doc. I've sketched a MAP outline below that ties evaluation gates to capacity reservations. I'm copying Marcus to add GPU sizing specifics.

MAP skeleton (proposal):
1) Discovery & sizing (2 weeks) — agree SLO targets, peak QPS, seq len distribution. No commit.
2) Eval sprint (4 weeks) — perf runs against a 2-node Dedicated pool (N1). If pass, customer signs intent to reserve tranche A (minimum 8xA100-equivalent slots).
3) Canary + integration (4 weeks) — roll to canary region, integration with KMS/audit logs. Reserve tranche B (additional 16 slots) if canary passes.
4) Production ramp (8 weeks) — staggered delivery of tranche C (bulk commit up to 48 slots) with options to accelerate subject to procurement lead time.

Key lead-time we call out: procurement and rack scheduling for Dedicated typically requires 10-12 weeks from paperwork to leased GPU availability for reserved pools (varies by region). Private (on-prem) varies widely — we need procurement calendar from your side.

Next steps: Marcus will propose a tranche-by-tranche GPU sizing and a compressed schedule option (if you need faster onboarding). I will produce a formal MAP doc (rdw-acme-map-v1.docx) and send for signature.

– Vivek
VP, Product Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: rdw-dedicated-onboard-checklist.xlsx

From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask — capacity runway and procurement lead times

Maria / team — quick GPU sizing proposal based on the traffic sketch you shared during the demo. If you can confirm average tokens per request and concurrency I'll refine these numbers.

Baseline assumptions (example):
- Avg tokens per request: 600
- Peak concurrent requests: 120
- Target p99 latency: <350ms
- Model: 13B quantized (compatible with our fast-path kernels)

Proposed tranches (A/B/C):
- Tranche A (eval): 8 slots (for short perf runs and stability tests)
- Tranche B (canary): +16 slots (canary at 20 slots total, supports low fan-out production tests)
- Tranche C (prod bulk): +48 slots (scales to sustained production; supports sharding and throughput)

Notes on lead times:
- Reserved Dedicated capacity provisioning (in-region) — estimate 10 weeks for initial 8-slot tranche, +4–6 weeks for incremental tranches depending on hardware sourcing windows.
- If Customer can accept multi-region split, we can reduce single-region procurement time but increase routing complexity.

I attached a quick csv with example capacity math (gpu-sizing-estimates.csv). Happy to set up a short workshop to finalize concurrency profiles.

– Marcus
Director, Serving Platform
Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Initial ask — capacity runway and procurement lead times

Hi all — adding the evaluation plan we typically include in MAPs. This is focused, measurable, and designed to minimize false negatives so procurement feels comfortable moving forward.

Eval plan (4-week sprint):
Week 0: onboarding — dataset ingest, access to audit logs, KMS testing.
Week 1: baseline perf runs — generate p50/p90/p99 curves across sample prompts.
Week 2: stress & stability — sustained runs at expected peak QPS for 4–6 hours, monitor KV cache hit rates and memory.
Week 3: integration gating — SSO, KMS, telemetry, and DR drills.

Gate criteria (pass -> reserve tranche A):
- p99 latency <= 400ms on target model under test harness
- No critical integration blockers (SSO, KMS, audit logging verified)
- Successful DR handoff and runbook review

Rollback and fallback: if any gate fails, we move to a remediation sprint and delay tranche reservation by the length of the sprint. If timing is critical we recommend a parallel soft-reserve (non-billed hold) while remediation occurs.

Attaching eval-cases.md with the checklist. Let me know if Acme needs any extra compliance checks included in the gate (PII scanning, custom retain/delete policies).

— Lauren
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple of updates from procurement:
- Capital approval window closes 2026-10-01; we need a signed intent and tranche schedule by 2026-09-15 to include in the request.
- On-prem vendor channel adds ~6 weeks to lead time; we can likely accept a mixed Dedicated + on-prem model but need clear delivery milestones.

Traffic clarifications:
- Expected peak QPS: ~150 (spiky), average concurrency ~75.
- Typical sequences: 400–900 tokens.

Given the approval window, is it possible to compress the MAP to a 6-week aggressive plan (2-week discovery + 2-week eval + 2-week canary) and put a soft reserve on tranche A while procurement completes paperwork? If so, please flag any risks.

Regards,
Maria

Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask — capacity runway and procurement lead times

Maria — thanks for the procurement window. We can support an accelerated MAP but there are trade-offs. Summary and next steps below.

Accelerated MAP (6-week aggressive):
- Week 0–1: Discovery & fast-scan (confirm concurrency and token mix).
- Week 2–3: Compressed eval sprint (parallelized perf runs using synthetic workload on a 10-slot eval pool).
- Week 4–5: Canary + integration (canary in a shadow region; integrate KMS and telemetry).

Commitments from Redwood:
- Soft reserve: we can place a non-billed hold on Tranche A (10 slots) for 30 days to align with your procurement window. This guarantees hardware availability for the aggressive path.
- Expedited provisioning support: priority provisioning queue if DocuSign + purchase order arrive within the hold window.
- Dedicated on-prem note: on-prem adds vendor/CSP rack lead time; we recommend keeping Tranche A in our Dedicated pool and adding an on-prem tranche later to avoid delays.

Risks:
- Compressed evals increase chance of false negatives (less time for stability runs). We mitigate with longer stress runs during the canary and a remediation sprint contingency in the MAP.
- Hardware sourcing volatility could shift incremental tranche dates by 2–4 weeks.

Action items (owners / dates):
- Vivek: send rdw-acme-map-v1.docx and soft-reserve agreement by 2026-08-19.
- Maria: confirm PO cadence and whether the 30-day soft hold aligns with procurement timelines by 2026-08-24.
- Marcus: schedule sizing workshop (30–60m) and deliver final gpu-sizing-estimates.csv by 2026-08-21.
- Lauren: prepare extended eval checklist for accelerated cadence by 2026-08-20.

If this looks good I'll open the soft reserve and route the MAP for signature.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Product Partnerships
Redwood Inference
